Qatar sees 'progress' in US-Iran talks after White House meeting
articles.summary: A day after Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Trump at the White House, a Qatari foreign ministry spokesman said both sides were making positive statements about a diplomatic solution but that “we cannot say how close or how far away an agreement is.”
articles.body: Qatar said on Tuesday it had seen “progress” in talks between the US and Iran, stating that Doha as a key mediator was “working tirelessly to end the uncertainty over the crisis between Washington and Tehran”.The assessment came a day after Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met US President Donald Trump at the White House.Al Hashmi said the White House meeting "was held in a positive atmosphere and was focused on making progress in the talks."“We cannot say how close or how far away an agreement is,” Ibrahim bin Sultan Al Hashmi, director of the foreign ministry’s Media and Communication Department, told a weekly briefing in Doha."We see that mediatory efforts continue, and both sides are making positive statements about a diplomatic solution," he added.He said Qatari officials had held talks in Tehran and consulted other governments in the region before Sheikh Mohammed travelled to Washington.Trump said Gulf states, including Qatar and Saudi Arabia, had urged him to hold off on fresh strikes. He said he would do so for now but keep the US naval blockade in place.Tehran has proposed resuming talks in as little as two days if Washington halts attacks, lifts its blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz and waives some sanctions. Negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme would come later.Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei defended the proposal on Monday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had dismissed some of Tehran’s conditions as “outrageous and ridiculous” the day before.Al Hashmi said the continued Hormuz closure would hit the most vulnerable hardest, calling for the strait — a key route for Gulf oil and liquefied natural gas exports — to reopen to shipping as soon as possible.Sheikh Mohammed joined ministers from Saudi Arabia, France, Britain, Germany and Italy in Paris on Tuesday to discuss the war on the sidelines of a G7 meeting.

articles.title: Trump says Iran war ‘effectively over’ as Tehran denies planned talks
articles.summary: Speaking after meeting Qatar’s prime minister, a key mediator, Trump said further strikes were “quite unlikely” but that the US was “locked and loaded”. Meanwhile, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei told Washington to stop “manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks”.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was momentum toward ending the war with Iran, as he declared that the country "militarily, is effectively over" but kept open the possibility of new strikes."Iran, militarily, is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo," Trump told reporters Monday at a White House press briefing. "But if we do have to go back in, we are locked and loaded, and ready to go."Trump met at the White House with Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, a key mediator in the Iran war, in his first meeting with a foreign leader since his party's massive losses in the midterm elections.Trump later posted on Truth Social that the two leaders had "an excellent conversation" and that "much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran."He said that Gulf states — Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and others — "preferred to the status quo" over strikes in what he described as "the largest naval blockade in history" and the Iron Gate land operation.He said all parties agreed Iran must not obtain a nuclear weapon and that the point was not open to negotiation, but again said further strikes were "quite unlikely"."We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this conflict, and will ensure that America's interests are at all times protected," Trump said.Qatar's Prime Minister Al Thani described his meeting with Trump and Vice President JD Vance in Washington as "excellent," saying they discussed "the situation in the region" and "ways to advance the negotiations between the United States and Iran."He said he was "grateful for the positive discussions on achieving an agreement and establishing peace in the region."Iron Gate is a CENTCOM task force created to block the transfer of advanced weapons, sanctioned goods and illicit revenues across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.Tehran pushes backIranian officials meanwhile expressed defiance at the continued pressure from Washington.Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei wrote on X late Monday that the US "flails like a desperate gambler," telling Washington to "fold your hand. Stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks."Earlier, Tehran's top negotiator Mahammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed on X that Israel was pushing the US deeper into conflict, adding that "unless Washington drops the 'Israel First' mindset, America and its allies are headed straight for a dark age."On the ground in Iran, strikes, which have not been publicly acknowledged by the US military, are continuing, according to Iranian authorities.The island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, was targeted overnight from Sunday to Monday, the provincial deputy governor stated on state television.Media outlets reported on Monday, citing Turkey's intelligence service chief Ibrahim Kalin, that Qatar would host a meeting between Vance and Rezaei next week. Kalin described it as an important opportunity for a breakthrough in the talks.Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied any such meeting was being planned. Tasnim news agency, citing a senior Iranian security official, said Iran's negotiating position had not changed and that it would not hold talks with the US until Washington took concrete steps within the framework of Iran's seven conditions.Brent crude futures fell to $92 a barrel on Monday as expectations grew that the war could end.

articles.title: UN Court Rejects Bosnian Serb War Criminal’s Early Release Plea Again
articles.summary: The court said former Bosnian Serb interior minister Mico Stanisic, who is serving 22 years in prison for war crimes, has failed to "sufficiently demonstrate rehabilitation".
articles.body: Mico Stanisic in court in The Hague in March 2005. Photo: EPA/Fred Ernst/Pool. The UN’s International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals in The Hague announced on Tuesday that it has denied early release to convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Mico Stanisic for a second time. Stanisic was the interior minister of Bosnia’s Serb-dominated entity, Republika Srpska, during Bosnia’s 1992-95 war. The Hague Tribunal sentenced him to 22 years in prison for persecution, murder and torture under a final verdict in 2016. Judge Graciela Gatti Santana, the president of the court, said that while Stanisic is eligible to be considered for early release after serving two-thirds of his sentence, there are “significant factors” militating against it. These include “the high gravity of his crimes and his failure to sufficiently demonstrate rehabilitation. Further, there is no evidence establishing the existence of compelling humanitarian grounds that would otherwise warrant overriding this negative assessment,” Gatti Santana added. He previously requested early release in November 2024 , but was turned down. His renewed request to the court in September this year stated that Stanisic served his sentence in a multi-ethnic prison and has had friendly relations with inmates of different ethnic backgrounds. It also noted that during his time in prison no disciplinary proceedings were brought against him. “The petitioner claims that, especially given the length of his sentence, his behaviour manifests a great level of re-socialisation,” the submission said. Responding to the submission, Gatti Santana said: “While Stanisic continues to exhibit good behaviour in detention and has maintained family relationships that would support his reintegration into society, the new evidence does not sufficiently address the concerns regarding his lack of acceptance of responsibility and critical reflection identified in the previous decision [in 2024].” Stanisic voluntarily surrendered to the Hague Tribunal in March 2005 and his trial began in September 2009, alongside his co-defandant, Stojan Zupljanin, the wartime head of the regional police centre in Banja Luka. Zupljanin was convicted of persecution, murder, torture and extermination.

articles.title: Gorduladze: Opposition trying to turn Constitutional Court proceedings into TV debates and a show
articles.summary: Archil Gordulაძე, Chairman of the Parliament's Legal Affairs Committee, has accused opposition representatives of attempting to turn the ongoing Constitutional Court proceedings into television debates and a show. Commenting on today's hearing, Gorduladze said representatives of what he described as unconstitutional parties were continuing their efforts to undermine the legal process through what he called demagoguery.
articles.body: Archil Gordulაძე, Chairman of the Parliament's Legal Affairs Committee, has accused opposition representatives of attempting to turn the ongoing Constitutional Court proceedings into television debates and a show. Commenting on today's hearing, Gorduladze said representatives of what he described as unconstitutional parties were continuing their efforts to undermine the legal process through what he called demagoguery. “They know that their unconstitutional actions have no legal justification, and now they are trying to get by solely through demagoguery,” Gorduladze said. He also criticized what he described as legally absurd demands, citing Nika Gvaramia's call for the Constitutional Court to adopt part of its final decision on the same day. “Such a thing has never been attempted, not only in the history of the Constitutional Court, but also in the history of the common courts and Georgian justice,” he said. Gorduladze added that when opposition parties lack legal grounds for their arguments, they resort either to legal nonsense as a lifeline or to what he described as actions dictated by those giving them instructions. articles.title: Coalition for Change asks Constitutional Court to delay enforcement of potential party ban by at least one month
articles.summary: The opposition Coalition for Change has filed a motion with Georgia’s Constitutional Court requesting that, if the Court rules in favor of banning political parties, the decision and its legal consequences take effect no earlier than one month after the ruling is announced.
articles.body: The opposition Coalition for Change has filed a motion with Georgia’s Constitutional Court requesting that, if the Court rules in favor of banning political parties, the decision and its legal consequences take effect no earlier than one month after the ruling is announced. Coalition for Change leader Nika Gvaramia claims that the motion concerns the timing of the enforcement of a potential ruling rather than the date of its announcement. The coalition is asking the Court to establish a single, unified date for the enforcement of any party ban and its associated legal consequences, including the cancellation of party registration under Article 23(3) of the Organic Law of Georgia on the Constitutional Court. The motion also requests that the Court clarify its position before the parties deliver their closing arguments, allowing them to take the Court’s response into account during the final stage of proceedings. Gvaramia stressed that submitting the motion does not mean the coalition expects the Court to uphold the claim or acknowledges any of the allegations against it. “The respondent’s position regarding the merits of the case remains unchanged: the claim against it is factually unsubstantiated and legally groundless, and therefore should not be granted. This motion does not imply an anticipation that the claim will be granted, nor does it constitute an admission of any circumstances,” Gvaramia said. Constitutional Court Judge Eva Gotsiridze questioned the legal rationale behind the request, suggesting that its purpose was to preserve the possibility of seeking interim measures from the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) under Rule 39. Gotsiridze explained that postponing the legal effects of Constitutional Court decisions is generally intended to prevent a legal vacuum, allowing lawmakers sufficient time to introduce replacement legislation when existing provisions are declared unconstitutional. However, she noted that the coalition’s request appeared to pursue a different objective: allowing the ECHR sufficient time to intervene before a potential party ban takes effect. “As I understand it, the objective is to ensure that the application of Rule 39 of the Rules of the European Court does not lose its effectiveness, allowing the European Court to issue a timely instruction to the Constitutional Court not to execute the decision,” Gotsiridze said. Rule 39 allows the European Court of Human Rights to indicate urgent interim measures to states in exceptional circumstances, particularly where there is a risk of serious and irreparable harm. The Constitutional Court has yet to announce a decision on the coalition’s motion, which seeks a ruling on the requested enforcement timeframe before the proceedings reach their final stage.

articles.title: Constitutional Court only partially grants Lelo's motion regarding examination of evidence during hearing
articles.summary: The Plenum of the Constitutional Court has only partially granted the motion filed by the political union of citizens Lelo – Strong Georgia regarding the examination of evidence during the hearing. The decision was communicated to the parties by the Chairman of the Constitutional Court, Revaz Nadaraia.
articles.body: The Plenum of the Constitutional Court has only partially granted the motion filed by the political union of citizens Lelo – Strong Georgia regarding the examination of evidence during the hearing. The decision was communicated to the parties by the Chairman of the Constitutional Court, Revaz Nadaraia. "The motion filed by the respondent party—the political union of citizens 'Lelo – Strong Georgia'—has been granted in part. The request to present every single internet link cited in the constitutional claim during the court proceedings is denied. Furthermore, the Court will not examine—during the hearing on the merits—facts that are 'generally known' (as per Article 31 of the Constitutional Court’s Regulations) or judicial acts that have already entered into legal force. During the course of the proceedings, the Court will assess the relevance of specific pieces of evidence cited in the claim—should their relevance be contested—either upon a substantiated motion from a party or on its own initiative. The ruling is final and is not subject to review or appeal. The Plenum was unanimous in adopting this ruling," stated Revaz Nadaraia. For context, "Lelo – Strong Georgia" had requested that an evidentiary hearing stage be conducted during the Constitutional Court’s proceedings regarding the lawsuit filed by "Georgian Dream" MPs, which seeks the banning of five opposition parties. This motion was submitted by Levan Samushia, representing the respondent side; however, representatives of other opposition parties also expressed their support for it.

articles.title: Hearings resume at Constitutional Court regarding potential ban of five opposition parties
articles.summary: The Constitutional Court has resumed hearings on a petition filed by Georgian Dream MPs seeking the banning of five opposition parties. The phase of the proceedings dedicated to opening statements and explanations has concluded; starting today, the Constitutional Court is moving on to the questioning stage.
articles.body: The Constitutional Court has resumed hearings on a petition filed by Georgian Dream MPs seeking the banning of five opposition parties. The phase of the proceedings dedicated to opening statements and explanations has concluded; starting today, the Constitutional Court is moving on to the questioning stage. As explained by the Chairman of the Constitutional Court, Revaz Nadaraia, the Court will first pose questions to the plaintiffs, followed by the respondents. For context, the Constitutional Court began reviewing the petition on October 21. The case is being heard by a plenum consisting of seven judges of the Constitutional Court. The petition submitted to the Constitutional Court is signed by 88 Members of Parliament. Based on their lawsuit, the court is set to consider the issue of declaring the following five political associations unconstitutional: "Unity – National Movement"; "Coalition for Change – Gvaramia, Melia, Girchi, Droa"; "Strong Georgia – Lelo, For the People, For Freedom!"; the "Federalist Party"; and the party "Gakharia for Georgia." The constitutional lawsuit is accompanied by the conclusion of a temporary investigative commission established within the 11th convocation of the Parliament.

articles.body: The US Department of Justice has brought charges against three Iranian and Iraqi nationals, APA reports. They are accused of plotting a terrorist attack in September 2026 on RAF Fairford, a British air base hosting US military forces. According to US authorities, the defendants supported the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah armed group and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). They are also suspected of involvement in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States.

articles.summary: Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change, said the decision had already been made and that the ongoing proceedings were merely an attempt to “whitewash” it, following the conclusion of a Constitutional Court hearing. articles.body: Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change, said the decision had already been made and that the ongoing proceedings were merely an attempt to “whitewash” it, following the conclusion of a Constitutional Court hearing. Gvaramia said the court had rejected a request to hold an evidentiary hearing, describing the decision as “absolutely unthinkable” and inconsistent with legal requirements. “What happened regarding the evidence is extremely problematic. I do not know how the court intends to get out of this situation. The entire stage of judicial examination has effectively been removed. This is absolutely unthinkable and does not comply with the requirements of the law,” Gvaramia said. He added that this was not the first time procedural fairness had worked against the opposition, claiming that the court had deprived the defendants of several procedural rights, including the opportunity to call witnesses and request evidence. “This really goes beyond everything. An entire stage has been removed altogether,” he said. Lelo - Strong Georgia had requested that the Constitutional Court hold an evidentiary hearing during proceedings on a lawsuit filed by Georgian Dream MPs seeking to ban five opposition parties. The motion was submitted by Levan Samushia, a representative of the respondent parties, and was supported by representatives of other opposition parties. The Constitutional Court's Plenum partially granted Lelo - Strong Georgia's motion to examine evidence during the hearing.

Serbia Prosecution Accused of Mishandling Cases of Anti-Govt Protesters
articles.summary: Report says it suspects Belgrade Prosecution 'committed criminal offences' in its handling of cases concerning anti-government protesters and the authorities' alleged use of a 'sound cannon' at a demonstration.
articles.body: A commission established by Serbia’s Supreme Public Prosecution Office said in a report published on Tuesday that the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade had committed irregularities in handling several high-profile cases. These cases relate to an alleged sonic weapon used during a huge anti-government protest in March 2025, as well as attacks on students and a police raid on the university rectorate building. “There are grounds to suspect that criminal offences falling under the jurisdiction of the Public Prosecutor’s Office for Organised Crime have been committed,” the commission said, adding that the report had been forwarded to the Prosecutor’s Office for the start of criminal proceedings. The commission was formed on October 27, two days after parliamentary elections in which the opposition Student List beat the Serbian Progressive Party, which had held power for 14 years. The report focused on seven cases at the Higher Prosecutor’s Office, and is likely just the first report. The report claims the head of the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade, Nenad Stefanovic, “instrumentalised certain public prosecutors in pursuit of illegitimate objectives, and effectively established a parallel prosecutorial system”. It says the commission had identified bias in the prosecution’s handling of cases, violations of the law through unlawful searches and seizures, and the collection of data unrelated to the subject matter of the proceedings. The commission also pointed to the alleged abuse of organisational and hierarchical powers, the use of prosecutorial authority against citizens and witnesses and restrictions on the exercise of the rights of injured parties. The ‘sonic weapon’ claims were made after around 300,000 people gathered at an anti-government protest in Belgrade in March 2025. During a 15-minute silence held in memory of the victims of the Novi Sad railway station disaster in 2024, protesters were suddenly startled by an unexpected noise and began running and screaming, triggering a brief stampede. A case was opened by the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office following complaints from protesters who suspected that a long-range acoustic weapon had been used. However, in September 2025, the prosecution decided that there were no grounds for criminal proceedings. The commission’s report said that numerous irregularities had occurred in the handling of the case, and the office had done less to investigate the incident and more to “formalise a decision, made in advance, that no sound cannon had been used”. According to the report, the prosecution treated claims by authorities that no acoustic weapon had been deployed as an indisputable fact, disregarding material evidence that directly contradicted them. “In several instances, the political affiliations of the authors of video recordings or critics were used as an argument against the credibility of their claims”, the report noted, referring to footage of the incident itself. The report also stated that, in June 2026, the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office asked Serbia’s Security Intelligence Agency, BIA, to conduct checks on 154 citizens who had given statements about the alleged use of a sound cannon. Following publication of the report, the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office said that it “rejects as unfounded the allegations contained in the report of the Supreme Public Prosecutor’s Office”. It questioned “whether the report was intended to examine the legality, effectiveness and consistency of the prosecution’s conduct, or whether it was in fact used as a means for the Supreme Public Prosecutor and certain prosecutors … to settle scores with the Chief Public Prosecutor and certain prosecutors of the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade”. On Tuesday, Stefanovic said he was filing a criminal complaint against Goran Ilic, a public prosecutor at the Supreme Public Prosecutor’s Office who chairs the commission. Stefanovic filed the complaint with the Public Prosecutor’s Office for Organised Crime, accusing Ilic of abuse of office and obstruction of justice, He alleges that Ilic interfered with the performance of his prosecutorial duties and advised him to resign.

articles.title: Albanian Talk Show Hosts Slam TV Regulator’s ‘Orwellian’ Fines
articles.summary: Sanctions imposed on several TV talk shows over language used by guests are raising concerns about restrictions about the right to freely debate the ongoing anti-government protests in Albania.
articles.body: Journalist Blendi Fevziu opened his TV programme “Opinion” last Thursday evening with a symbolic protest. Wearing a uniform bearing the inscription “AMA Police”, Fevziu mocked the imposition of a fine for “content containing inappropriate language” imposed by the Audiovisual Media Authority, AMA – the body regulating television broadcasts in Albania. “I am not complaining about the fine but about the fact that, after 30 years in this studio ... they want to turn my normal attire into the uniform of an AMA police officer,” Fevziu said. “I am no longer supposed to be a journalist moderating a debate between two balanced sides or discussing a topic with different perspectives. Instead, I am supposed to be a police officer standing here to check and certify every word spoken by every guest, reprimanding them if it is deemed inappropriate,” he added. articles.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov officially files for a second term in 2027
articles.summary: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has submitted his documents to the Central Election Commission (CEC) to register as a candidate in the upcoming presidential election. The incumbent leader intends to seek a second term, Kaktus.media reported.
articles.body: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has submitted his documents to the Central Election Commission (CEC) to register as a candidate in the upcoming presidential election. The incumbent leader intends to seek a second term, Kaktus.media reported. He previously won the snap presidential election on Jan. 10, 2021, securing 79.2% of the vote. He officially assumed office on Jan. 28, 2021. Previously, the president was elected for a six-year term. However, following the adoption of a new Constitution in 2021, the presidential term was shortened to five years, with the possibility of serving two consecutive terms. To qualify as a presidential candidate, an individual must be a Kyrgyz citizen aged at least 35 and collect at least 30,000 supporting signatures. Candidates must also pay an electoral deposit of 1 million soms and submit a certificate confirming that they have passed the Kyrgyz language proficiency examination, known as the Kyrgyztest, at an above-average level. They must also provide documentation confirming that they do not hold citizenship of another country. In addition to Japarov, five other individuals have submitted their documents to the CEC: Aymen Kasenov , Azamat Esenbekov , Syimyk Japykeev , Akai Kydyrov , Iskhak Masaliev .

Russian presidential envoy thanks Kushner, Witkoff for facilitating Trump’s peace effort
articles.summary: MOSCOW, November 11. Russian Presidential Special Representative for Investment and Economic Cooperation with Foreign Countries and Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF) CEO Kirill Dmitriev thanked US special presidential envoy Steve Witkoff and the US president’s son-in-law Jared Kushner for their effort to promote Donald Trump’s Ukraine peace plan.
articles.body: MOSCOW, November 11. /TASS/. Russian Presidential Special Representative for Investment and Economic Cooperation with Foreign Countries and Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF) CEO Kirill Dmitriev thanked US special presidential envoy Steve Witkoff and the US president’s son-in-law Jared Kushner for their effort to promote Donald Trump’s Ukraine peace plan. "Thank you, Jared and Steve, for all of your hard work to advance President Trump’s peace plan. Peacemakers will prevail. Warmongers and their ubiquitous bots will lose," he wrote on the X social network. Negotiations between Russia, the United States and Ukraine on a Ukrainian settlement are being held on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi. Russian Presidential Aide Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russian delegation, while Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov heads Ukraine’s team. Witkoff, Kushner, Commander-in-Chief of NATO forces in Europe Alexus Grynkewich and UAE Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan were also present at the negotiating table at the time of their start. Contrary to remarks made by French officials, no European delegates were present. Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated earlier the negotiations would focus on security guarantees.

articles.body: ABU DHABI, November 10. /TASS/. The Russian delegation at the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi is not making any statements to the press on Tuesday but will hold an official press conference on Wednesday, TASS reported citing a source in the negotiating team at the talks. The two-day talks kicked off on Tuesday at about 8:15 a.m. GMT. The Russian and Ukrainian delegations were seated opposite each other at a U-shaped table. The first day of talks lasted four hours and 30 minutes with a 40-minute break. Negotiations between Russia, the United States and Ukraine on a Ukrainian settlement are being held on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi. Russian Presidential Aide Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russian delegation, while Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov heads Ukraine’s team.
